proposal: The Mandate recommends returning to prior policy by implementing an industry-recognized apprenticeship program (IRAP) separate from the Registered Apprenticeship Program, exploring how to modernize, streamline and remove duplication in the registered program, and asking Congress to re-create the IRAP system by statute so that trade associations and educational institutions can recognize and oversee apprenticeships. It also urges DOL and the NLRB to make it easier for religious organizations to take part in apprenticeship programs.

status_summary: No revival of industry-recognized apprenticeship programs was found; the administration's actions have centered on the registered program. Executive Order 14278 (signed 2025-04-23) ordered a plan to reach and surpass 1 million new active apprentices, including by expanding Registered Apprenticeship into new industries, and does not mention industry-recognized programs or religious organizations. DOL proposed on 2025-07-02 (90 FR 28947) to rescind the affirmative action program requirements of the registered program's equal-opportunity rules and to refer discrimination complaints to enforcement agencies; DOL's August 2026 regulatory agenda still lists the rulemaking at the proposed rule stage, and no final rule appeared in the Federal Register through 2026-10-19. A trade article reports DOL awarded $84 million in apprenticeship grants to all states and territories around June 2025.

timeline.event: President signs EO 14278, Preparing Americans for High-Paying Skilled Trade Jobs of the Future (published 2025-04-28). Section 4 directs the Secretaries of Labor, Commerce and Education to produce a plan within 120 days to reach and surpass 1 million new active apprentices, including extending Registered Apprenticeship to new industries; section 3 orders a review of federal workforce programs. The order does not mention industry-recognized apprenticeships.

According to ACHR News, which cites a DOL release of 2025-06-30, DOL awards $84 million in apprenticeship grants to every state and territory for starting programs, modernizing training and recruiting apprentices.

DOL's Employment and Training Administration proposes Prohibiting Illegal Discrimination in Registered Apprenticeship Programs (90 FR 28947; RIN 1205-AC21). It would rescind the affirmative action program provisions of 29 CFR part 30, including utilization analyses and goals, and refer discrimination complaints to the EEOC or state agencies; DOL says the burdens deter employers, especially small businesses, from registering programs. Comments closed 2025-09-02 (382 comments).

title: Re-create industry-recognized apprenticeships and streamline Registered Apprenticeship
uncertainties: The absence of an industry-recognized apprenticeship revival rests on a Federal Register API query for the phrase industry recognized apprenticeship (zero results since 2025-01-20, rerun 2026-10-18), the text of Executive Order 14278 (read in full) and DOL's regulatory agenda. A Federal Register API query of Department of Labor apprenticeship documents since 2026-06-01, run 2026-10-18, returned 12 documents through 2026-10-19 with no final nondiscrimination rule and no IRAP document; a rule at OIRA would not appear there. DOL's own apprenticeship pages and the 120-day plan were not located, and congress.gov (which could not be opened) and govinfo were not searched for IRAP bills. The $84 million grant figure is a secondary trade report. A trade report that the Labor Secretary nominee said at her confirmation hearing that IRAP discussions had not taken place, and the agenda listing of the rulemaking, are kept as sources but are not government actions, so they are no longer timeline events. The proposed rule page was read only to about 100,000 of 127,000 characters. The Mandate's interest in religious organizations' participation has no identified government action. Whether the proposed part 30 rule counts as the streamlining half of the recommendation is a judgment, since DOL framed it around nondiscrimination law.
